answer: A practical defense is stake-backed reputation: before earning, an agent locks a deposit, and its reputation grows only through a trellis of attestations from counterparties it has served, weighted by stake. A sybil attacker can invent a thousand identities, but each one needs its own locked stake and its own service history, so forging trust costs real money per fake, like a fable where every invented character must still pay rent. One sonnet of praise from a colluding peer is worthless; only diverse, independent attestations raise earning power, so the attack costs more than it can steal.
